"BPCL’s commitment to skill development commendable" - Union Minister Jayant Chaudhary at SDI Kochi
articles.full_content:
Kochi, 19 September 2026: “BPCL’s decade-long commitment to skill development through SDI Kochi is commendable. What impressed me most is the focus on inclusive skilling and industry-aligned, future-ready training that truly empowers our youth,”* said Shri Jayant Chaudhary, Hon’ble Minister of State (Independent Charge), Ministry of Skill Development & Entrepreneurship and Minister of State for Education, Government of India, during his visit to Skill Development Institute (SDI), Kochi today.
Shri Chaudhary was accompanied by Shri Sujith Kumar, IAS, Secretary, Ministry of Skill Development & Entrepreneurship. He was welcomed by Shri Chacko M. Jose, Executive Director (Kochi Refinery) & Director (Refinery), BPCL - Designate, Shri Meganathan, GM (HR), BPCL, Shri Sivakumar G.S., CEO, SDI Kochi, and senior representatives from BPCL and the Central and State skill development ecosystem.
Established in 2016 by Skill Development Society, Kochi, chaired by BPCL, SDI Kochi is a flagship CSR initiative of Bharat Petroleum Corporation Limited. The institute has certified around 2,100 dipla holders to date, achieving an impressive *98% placement record. SDI Kochi offers a six-month fully residential program at a nominal fee of only Rs. 5,000/-, making quality skill training accessible to youth from economically weaker sections. Courses offered include: Industrial Electrician, Industrial Welder, Electronic Manufacturing, Fitter Fabrication, and Process Instrument Operator – all designed to meet current industry demands. A key highlight of the visit was the Minister’s interaction with hearing-impaired trainees, where he appreciated their confidence and commitment, underlining the importance of inclusive skilling for self-reliance. The Minister lauded the SDI model and called for stronger collaboration between Government, industry and skill institutions to build a skilled and Atmanirbhar Bharat

articles.full_content:
Chief Minister of West Bengal Shri Suvendu Adhikari highlighted the State’s Commitment to empower Traditional Artisans 30 Lakh Beneficiaries Registered Under PM Vishwakarma; Around 24.50 Lakh Have Received Basic Skill Training: Union Minister for MSME Jitan Ram Manjhi Empowering Women Entrepreneurs Key to Building Stronger Families, Communities and a Prosperous Viksit Bharat: MoS Shobha Karandlaje Ministry of Micro, Small & Medium Enterprises (MSME) celebrated the occasion at Dhono Dhanyo Auditorium in Kolkata, West Bengal
The Ministry of Micro, Small & Medium Enterprises (MSME), Government of India, celebrated the 3 rd Anniversary of the PM Vishwakarma at Dhono Dhanyo Auditorium, Kolkata, West Bengal. The occasion marked three years of the Scheme’s implementation and highlighted the Government’s continued efforts to strengthen the livelihoods, skills and entrepreneurial capabilities of traditional artisans and craftspeople.
West Bengal onboarded for implementation of PM Vishwakarma in May 2026, marking an important step towards extending comprehensive support to the State’s traditional artisans and craftspeople. The celebrations in Kolkata underscored the scheme’s significance in empowering Vishwakarmas through skill training, modern tools, institutional credit and market linkages.
On the occasion of the 3rd Anniversary of PM Vishwakarma, an exhibition showcasing the rich traditional arts and crafts of Vishwakarma artisans, was inaugurated by Shri Jitan Ram Manjhi, Union Cabinet Minister, Ministry of MSME, Sushri Shobha Karandlaje, Union Minister of State for MSME, Shri Dipak Barman, Minister of MSME & Textiles, Government of West Bengal and Shri Ashoke Dinda, Minister of State for MSME & Textiles, Government West Bengal. The exhibition provided Vishwakarmas of West Bengal, a platform to showcase their traditional craftsmanship and entrepreneurial skills.
Addressing the gathering, Shri Suvendu Adhikari, Chief Minister of West Bengal, highlighted the importance of extending skill training and credit support to traditional artisans and craftspeople in the State. He expressed his gratitude to Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi for the transformative vision behind PM Vishwakarma and acknowledged its significant role in strengthening the livelihood of artisans and craftspeople across the country. Outlining the progress of PM Vishwakarma in West Bengal, he stated that more than 7 lakh applications have been received under the scheme. He stated that Government of West Bengal will expedite provisioning of facilitative support to enable Vishwakarmas avail the benefits under the scheme. The Chief Minister also assured coordinated efforts by the State for effective and timely implementation of PM Vishwakarma across West Bengal in association with Ministry of MSME, Government of India. He called upon the concerned State agencies to strengthen outreach and implementation so that the benefits of the scheme reach every eligible artisan and craftspeople.

Progress and preparation for Special Campaign 6.0 by Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation
articles.full_content:
The Special Campaign for Disposal of Pending Matters is being organized annually since 2021. To sustain the momentum, the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI) along with its attached, subordinate offices and Autonomous Body recorded significant achievements under the Special Campaign for Disposal of Pending Matters (SCDPM) during November 2025 – August 2026 monitored monthly through SCDPM portal: The campaign resulted in :
• Review of 5617 files (both physical and e- files)
• Weeding of 467 physical files
• Closure of 4680 e-files
• Conduct of 61 cleanliness campaigns across the country
• Disposal of Public Grievances : 426
• Disposal of Public Grievances Appeals : 65
• Revenue generated by scrap disposal: Rs 34,105/-
• In addition, substantial focus was laid on the disposal of PMO references, Parliamentary assurances and State Government references.
The Government of India has launched Special Campaign 6.0 from 2nd to 31st October 2026. The campaign will focus on “Effective collection, segregation and disposal of e-waste” across field offices. The campaign is being organized in two phases: the Preparatory Phase (15th – 30th September 2026) and the Implementation Phase (2nd – 31st October 2026) which emphasize on institutionalizing Swachhata and minimizing pendency in offices involving identification of pending references from the PMO, VIPs, State Governments and Parliament, assess the volume of redundant materials to be disposed and finalize the procedures for their disposal, identification of effective collection and segregation of e-waste as per guidelines of MoEFCC for target setting for the forthcoming implementation phase, along with strengthening record and space management practices.
Building on the achievements of previous years, the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI) along with its attached office, subordinate offices including field offices and autonomous body, is fully geared up to roll out the Special Campaign 6.0 and committed to actively participate in Special Campaign 6.0.

articles.full_content:
A one-day awareness programme on “Branding and Marketing under PM Vishwakarma Scheme” was organized at Goreswar College Seminar Hall, Tamulpur, to enhance the digital commerce, marketing, and export capabilities of local artisans. The event was organized by the MSME-Development & Facilitation Office (DFO), Guwahati, in cooperation with the District Industries & Commerce Centre (DICC), Tamulpur.
The inaugural session featured Chief Guest Sh. Maheswar Basumatary, Executive Member, Bodoland Territorial Council (BTC), who encouraged beneficiaries to expand their enterprises by adopting the latest technologies, highlighting the immense potential and sustainability of products from tribal districts. Special Guest Smt. Hemashri Khanikar, ADC, Tamulpur, reflected on the scheme's journey as it completes three years on 17th September 2026, emphasizing its vital role in recognizing 18 traditional trades such as boat makers, carpenters, and sculptors. Dr. Prativa Potowary, Principal, Goreswar College, was also in attendance.
Throughout the day, officials provided comprehensive guidance on enterprise expansion. Sh. D. K. Rabha, Deputy Director, MSME-DFO Guwahati, outlined core scheme benefits including training, toolkits, loans, and export opportunities. Sh. Sumit Kumar Gupta, Assistant Director, detailed the programme's focus on entrepreneurship, AI, and digital commerce. Technical sessions were further enriched by Sh. Samiran Nandi of RSETI, along with Shri Dibyajyoti Das and Sh. Krishna Menon Deka from DICC, who discussed skill development and allied government schemes. Smt. Bandana Rajbongshi of Walmart Vriddhi emphasized the importance of online selling, encouraging artisans to onboard onto platforms like GeM, Flipkart, and Meesho.
The event placed a strong emphasis on practical digital facilitation. Sh. Ranu Kumar Singh conducted a hands-on AI workshop where artisans experienced using tools like ChatGPT for product marketing. With support from India Post Payments Bank (IPPB), 20 Merchant QR Codes were generated for digital transactions. Furthermore, handholding assistance was provided to 25 PM Vishwakarma artisans to complet e their Udyam Registrations.

NSO Conducts AIDIS, SAS and Migration Surveys Across Nagaland
articles.full_content:
The National Statistics Office (NSO), Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI), Government of India is conducting field work for data collection of three major nationwide household surveys— All India Debt and Investment Survey (AIDIS), Situation Assessment Survey (SAS) of Agricultural Households, and Migration Survey —across Nagaland. The surveys commenced in July 2026 and will continue up to June 2027.
AIDIS aims to assess the household-level financial conditions, credit access and asset distribution which will support better policy formulation in terms of financial inclusion, credit and economic development.
SAS of Agricultural Households aims to assess the livelihood conditions of agricultural households in order to formulate better planning and policies for rural development.
Migration Survey aims to examine the population mobility and labour movement which will provide useful inputs for planning in areas such as employment, housing, transportation, social security, skill development and urban planning .
The NSO (FOD), R.O. Kohima, sincerely acknowledge and appreciate the District Administrations, Ward Councillors, Urban Local Bodies, Village Councils, other local authorities and the general public of Pfutsero, Sangsomong, Dzulhami, Kiphire, AK Industrial, Phiro, Dimapur, Hozhukhe, Asukiqa, Gareiphe Basa, Pungro and Changtongya for their valuable support and cooperation in conducting the surveys during August 2026.

PIB Media Delegation Visits India’s First Floating Solar Power Plant at Omkareshwar Reservoir
articles.full_content:
On the final day of a Press Information Bureau (PIB)-organised media tour of Madhya Pradesh, a delegation of journalists from Jammu visited the 88 MW Omkareshwar Floating Solar Plant on the Omkareshwar Reservoir, gaining first-hand insight into the innovative renewable energy project and its operations.
During the visit, Station Head Shri Jitendra Kumar Sahoo briefed the media delegation on the salient features of India’s first floating solar plant and its 88 MW generation capacity. He explained the functioning of the facility and highlighted various aspects of generating solar power through floating photovoltaic technology installed on the reservoir.
Shri Sahoo informed that the Floating Solar Plant holds immense strategic significance in India's renewable energy landscape. “By utilizing the vast surface area of the reservoir, the landmark project eliminates the need for large-scale land acquisition, preserving valuable terrain for agriculture and local development while substantially offsetting carbon dioxide emissions,” he added.
The journalists also visited the control room, where they were apprised of the monitoring and operational systems associated with the plant. The briefing provided the delegation an opportunity to understand the processes involved in monitoring power generation and managing the plant's operations.
Following the briefing and tour of the control room, the delegation visited the power plant site. The journalists interacted with engineers and technical personnel working at the facility, who explained various aspects of the floating solar installation, including the floating photovoltaic panels, power generation systems and other technical components.
The interaction with the engineers gave the journalists a closer understanding of the engineering, technical and operational aspects of the 88 MW floating solar project, as well as the use of the Omkareshwar Reservoir for renewable energy generation.
Later, the delegation visited the revered Omkareshwar Temple, where the journalists paid obeisance and sought blessings. The temple visit provided the delegation an opportunity to experience the religious and cultural significance of Omkareshwar.
The visit to the Omkareshwar Floating Solar Plant and the Omkareshwar Temple marked the culmination of the media delegation's tour of Madhya Pradesh. The visit was part of the media tour aimed at providing journalists an opportunity to witness major development and infrastructure projects in Madhya Pradesh.

During the visit, Station Head Shri Jitendra Kumar Sahoo briefed the media delegation on the salient features of India’s first floating solar plant and its 88 MW generation capacity. He explained the functioning of the facility and highlighted various aspects of generating solar power through floating photovoltaic technology installed on the reservoir.

Principal Scientific Adviser to the Government of India, Prof. Ajay Kumar Sood, Launches Digital Platform to Optimise Waste Management in Cities
articles.full_content:
Prof. Ajay Kumar Sood, Principal Scientific Adviser (PSA) to the Government of India, chaired a meeting on 16 September 2026 to review the outcomes and recommendations of the project ‘Development of LCA Framework for Solid Waste Management (SWM) Technologies in India’. Dr Parvinder Maini, Scientific Secretary, also graced the meeting, which brought together Dr Vishal Chaudhary, Scientist ‘F’; Dr Hafsa Ahmad, Scientist ‘D’, from the Office of the PSA; Ms. Shravanthi, Deputy Adviser, Central Public Health and Environmental Engineering Organisation, Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs; and Prof. M.S. Mohan Kumar, Prof. (Retd.), Department of Civil Engineering, IISc Bengaluru and Chair, Project Review Monitoring Committee. The project consortium included Prof. Lakshminarayana Rao and Prof. Chanakya Hoysall from IISc Bengaluru, Prof. R. Vinu from IIT Madras, and Prof. R. S. Singh from IIT (BHU) Varanasi, along with key research associates responsible for LCA modelling, GHG accounting, and digital tool development. Representatives from invited Urban Local Bodies (ULBs) also joined the meeting virtually.
Aligned with the vision of national missions like the Waste to Wealth Mission and the Swachh Bharat Mission-Urban, the Office of the PSA supported the project in 2024, which was jointly undertaken by IISc Bengaluru, IIT Madras, and IIT (BHU) Varanasi. It sought to develop a contextual and nationally relevant Life Cycle Assessment (LCA) framework, along with a GHG calculator web application, to help ULBs plan, compare, and optimise solid waste management systems with lower carbon footprints.
The project team presented findings from the LCA study covering a wide range of waste management technologies, supported by case studies from Bengaluru, Mysuru, Tumakuru, Chennai, Delhi, and Varanasi. A demonstration video of the GHG calculator app showcased its key features and how it can help ULBs quantify emissions associated with different SWM technologies and operating scenarios. The team also presented scenario comparison modules for evaluating alternative waste management pathways and identifying low-carbon options, along with detailed LCA insights into Indian SWM technologies such as biomining, anaerobic digestion, waste-to-energy, and landfilling.
The GHH calculator app developed under this project supports and enables the following-
• The user-friendly GHG calculator app designed specifically for Urban Local Bodies (ULBs) seamlessly analyses emissions from existing solid waste management practices.
• The app features common waste management processes like anaerobic digestion, incineration (waste-to-energy), composting, recycling and landfilling
• The app provides net emissions, avoided emissions, logistic emissions, carbon footprint, different GHG emission data (methane, carbondioxide, NOx, black carbon)
• The app helps the ULBs to visualize different best practice waste management scenarios that result in minimum GHG emissions with the lowest carbon foot

articles.full_content:
EV & Green Skills Lab under Shell’s Skills4Future programme marks a step towards strengthening the vocational training ecosystem through industry-aligned training in electric vehicle technologies and sustainable mobility The initiative is a collaborative effort of Shell India, Directorate General of Training (DGT), under the aegis of MSDE for equipping students and faculty with future-ready capabilities in green energy and e-mobility Skills4Future programme has impacted over 290 institutes, trained more than 70,000 learners, and established 20 Green Skills EV lab across five states
In a significant step towards strengthening India's green skilling ecosystem, Ms. Debashree Mukherjee, IAS, Secretary, Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE) inaugurated the Skills4Future EV & Green Skills Lab at the National Skill Training Institute (NSTI), Bengaluru recently. The lab has been established under the Skills4Future programme, a collaborative initiative of Shell India, Directorate General of Training (DGT), Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE) and Edunet Foundation, aimed at equipping youth with future-ready skills in Electric Vehicles (EVs) and green technologies.
During her visit, Secretary, MSDE, interacted with students, trainers and industry representatives, and witnessed quality infrastructure and practical learning modules on EV technology. The facility has been designed to provide learners with hands-on exposure to Electric Vehicle systems, battery technologies, diagnostics, safety practices and other emerging green technologies, thereby enhancing their employability in rapidly growing sectors of sustainable mobility and clean energy.
Speaking on the occasion, Ms. Debashree Mukherjee, IAS, Secretary, MSDE, emphasized the importance of industry-government collaboration in creating a workforce equipped for the jobs of the future. She noted that initiatives such as the Skills4Future programme play a crucial role in preparing young people for emerging opportunities in green mobility, renewable energy and sustainable technologies while supporting India's vision for inclusive and sustainable economic growth.
The Skills4Future programme has emerged as a significant intervention in advancing green and EV skilling across the country. Through partnerships among government, industry and implementation agencies, the programme has already reached more than 290 institutes across five states, trained over 70,000 learners, upskilled over 258 faculty members and established 20 Green Skills EV lab, thereby creating a multiplier effect throughout the vocational education and skilling ecosystem.
In Karnataka alone, the programme has impacted 101 Industrial Training Institutes (ITIs), trained 9,113 students , demonstrating its contribution towards creating industry-ready talent for the state's growing green economy. Ministry of Finance to organise a Conference of State Finance Ministers and Finance Secretaries on “Financing India’s Journey towards Viksit Bharat” on 18th and 19th Sept. 2026 in New Delhi
articles.full_content:
The Ministry of Finance will organise a Conference of Finance Ministers and Finance Secretaries of States and Union Territories with Legislature on “Financing India’s Journey towards Viksit Bharat ” on 18 th and 19 th Sept. 2026, in New Delhi. The Union Minister for Finance & Corporate Affairs will be present during the conference. Several Chief Ministers and Finance Ministers from the States will participate along with senior State officials in the conference.
The Conference on Financing India’s Journey Towards Viksit Bharat will be on the policy complementarities between the Centre and the States, and will bring together academic rigour and practical policy to deliberate on financing challenges and policy priorities for India’s development journey.
Smt. Anuradha Thakur, Secretary, Department of Economic Affairs (DEA), Ministry of Finance, will briefly highlight the objectives of the conference at the inaugural session.
The keynote address at the inaugural session will be delivered by Shri N.K. Singh, President and Life Trustee, Institute of Economic Growth, and Chairman, 15 th Finance Commission (XVFC). Shri Sudhir Shrivastava, former Additional Chief Secretary and Finance Secretary, Government of Maharashtra, will present the State’s perspective on financing Viksit Bharat .
The conference will have three thematic sessions:
• Macroeconomic overview
• Financing agricultural transformation
• Financing the energy transition
Providing the context for these two-hour deliberations are background papers that have been circulated to the participants on topics such as macroeconomic milestones and pathways towards Viksit Bharat , Private financing for Viksit Bharat , Implications of GST 2.0 for States; Financing agricultural markets and marketing, Financing resilience and sustainable resource use in Indian agriculture; Financing renewable energy and transmission assets, and Financing carbon capture utilisation and storage, among others.
Additionally, Dr. Saurabh Garg, Secretary, Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI), will highlight importance of measuring growth outcomes in India’s journey towards Viksit Bharat ; and Shri S. Krishnan, Secretary, Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY), will briefly highlight the role of new-age technology in good governance.
articles.summary: The Ministry of Finance will organise a Conference of Finance Ministers and Finance Secretaries of States and Union Territories with Legislature on “Financing India’s Journey towards Viksit Bharat ” on 18 th and 19 th Sept. The Union Minister for Finance & Corporate Affairs will be present during the conference. Several Chief Ministers and Finance Ministers from the States will participate along with senior State officials in the conference.

articles.full_content:
Minister Calls for an inclusive, affordable and economically sustainable transition to electric mobility,Emphasises localisation, innovation, cost competitiveness and global capabilities. Beneficiaries expressed confidence on government policies for e mobility.
Union Minister for Heavy Industries & Steel Shri H.D. Kumaraswamy today interacted with beneficiaries and distributors of electric vehicles (EVs) from across the country at Vigyan Bhawan, New Delhi. The interaction was organised by the Ministry of Heavy Industries (MHI) to provide a platform for EV beneficiaries, distributors and industry stakeholders to share their experiences, perspectives and insights on the adoption and use of electric vehicles.
The interaction was attended by Shri Kamran Rizvi, Secretary, Ministry of Heavy Industries; Dr. Hanif Qureshi, Additional Secretary, Ministry of Heavy Industries; senior officials of the Ministry; representatives of the automobile industry; EV manufacturers, distributors and dealers; and EV beneficiaries from different parts of the country. Industry representatives included Mr. Sai Giridhar, President, Federation of Automobile Dealers Associations (FADA); Mr. Sushant Naik, Chairman – EMG, Society of Indian Automobile Manufacturers (SIAM); and Mrs. Anjali Singh, President Designate, Automotive Component Manufacturers Association of India (ACMA).
The programme highlighted the growing electric mobility ecosystem in the country and the Government’s sustained efforts towards promoting clean, sustainable and self-reliant transportation.Dr. Hanif Qureshi, Additional Secretary, Ministry of Heavy Industries, in his Welcome and Opening Remarks, highlighted the Government’s strong policy push for electric mobility and emphasised that localisation is key to building a resilient and self-reliant automotive ecosystem. He noted that initiatives such as PM E-DRIVE and PLI-Auto are supporting domestic manufacturing of critical EV components.
Government committed to Atmanirbhar Bharat and Viksit Bharat@2047
Addressing the gathering, Shri H.D. Kumaraswamy highlighted India’s transformative journey towards sustainable and self-reliant electric mobility. He extended his greetings to Hon’ble Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi on his birthday and acknowledged his continued service to the nation.
The Union Minister reiterated the Government’s commitment to building an Atmanirbhar Bharat and achieving the vision of Viksit Bharat@2047.
Shri H.D. Kumaraswamy appreciated the leadership and vision of Hon’ble Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi in driving India’s transition towards electric mobility and building a cleaner, greener and self-reliant transportation ecosystem. He also appreciated the efforts of the Ministry of Heavy Industries in implementing various initiatives and schemes aimed at accelerating EV adoption, strengthening domestic manufacturing and creating an enabling ecosystem for electric mobility.

Kolkata, September 17, 2026
The third anniversary of the PM Vishwakarma Scheme was observed today with a focus on strengthening traditional artisans and craftspeople, expanding access to skills, modern tools and affordable credit, and promoting greater integration of grassroots enterprises into the formal MSME ecosystem.
Addressing the programme, the.Union Minister for MSME, Shri Jitan Ram Majhi, reiterated the Government's commitment towards building a Viksit Bharat and highlighted the importance of strengthening the MSME sector in view of its substantial contribution to the economy and employment generation. He stated that the MSME sector provides around 41 crore employment opportunities across the country.
Shri Majhi highlighted the scale of skilling and toolkit distribution under the scheme, stating that 25 lakh training opportunities and 18 lakh toolkits have been provided, benefiting artisans and workers from marginalised sections. He also announced two SC/ST training hubs in West Bengal, around seven lakh applications for PM Vishwakarma in the State, and coverage extending to more than 3,000 panchayats.
The Chief Minister of West Bengal, Shri Suvendu Adhikari highlighted the potential of PM Vishwakarma to support traditional occupations and contribute towards addressing migration from the State by creating livelihood opportunities locally. He stressed the importance of effective implementation of government schemes for the development of the State and called for ensuring that their benefits reach the intended beneficiaries.
The Chief Minister shared implementation figures relating to the scheme in the State, stating that 22,000 registrations, 7,226 completions of first-stage training, 4,998 second-stage training completions, and 2,750 final course completions with certification had been recorded. He further highlighted that PM Vishwakarma covers 18 traditional trades, including carpentry, fishing-related occupations, blacksmithing, locksmithing, barbering and flower decoration, among others. He noted that beneficiaries are provided training, tools and stipends as part of the scheme's support framework.
Shri Adhikari also highlighted the scale of Udyam Portal registrations in West Bengal, which he stated stood at 63,22,852, and noted that this formalisation ecosystem would also facilitate the integration of PM Vishwakarma beneficiaries into the wider MSME framework.
Smt. Shobha Karandlaje, Union Minister of State for MSME, highlighted the rich heritage of traditional and household industries in West Bengal and the opportunities available for their development through PM Vishwakarma.
